execution.actorAExecutions: separate control and treatment subagent executions launched to work concurrently

question: Does a machine-readable signal about evolving producer-interface work help an independent consumer actor produce work that passes integration against the actual interface candidate before corrective feedback?
hypothesis: The relevant prospective work signal lets a consumer actor choose an implementation compatible with an evolving interface and avoid an integration correction.

preregistration.primaryMetric: Binary first-pass integration validation of the unchanged consumer commit applied atop the exact producer candidate, before integration-error feedback.
limitations: One actor execution per condition cannot establish statistical superiority or population-level causality.
The signal was hand-authored from declared intent and updated from observed Git/Artifact state; signal generation and relevance selection were not tested.
The experiment tests one async interface dependency in a small deterministic fixture, not general engineering quality.

primaryResult.interpretation: OBSERVED in this paired fixture: the treated candidate was compatible before integration feedback; the control candidate required one correction. This is consistent with the hypothesis, but the small sample and unknown actor profiles prevent a general causal claim.

methodAndToolingNotes: The fixture package has no declared local TypeScript compiler dependency. The experiment pinned its validation command to TypeScript 5.9.3 through npm exec; a plain npm run build therefore fails on a clean clone unless TypeScript is supplied. This is a fixture reproducibility limitation, not a collaboration result.

The first Actor B push harness completed the Git push and token revocation but errored before printing its readback because EXPERIMENT_AUTH_FILE was not passed to that one-off process. The independent Worker readback was immediately repeated successfully; no credential was exposed.

A direct `cf artifacts ... repos create` attempt returned HTTP 401 even though `cf auth whoami` was authenticated. The repository setup used the already qualified Worker binding fork path; exact cause of the CLI/API discrepancy remains UNKNOWN.
No Artifact events were configured or claimed.
